title: Agentic engineering loop
lede: Every piece of work enters through an intake, becomes a spec folder, and moves through the loop with a gate at each step. This page shows the loop, how work enters it, and where every piece of work is now.

intake.title: Idea
intake.what: A plain description, no ticket yet

intake.title: GitHub issue or bug
intake.what: A bug or request raised on a repo

intake.title: Pull request to review
intake.what: Code someone wrote, reviewed against the spec

phases.title: Intent
phases.does: Sources into inputs/, then why, for whom, outcome, success measures. /gap maps it onto existing code.

phases.title: Spec
phases.does: One requirement per behaviour, Given/When/Then acceptance criteria.
phases.gate: Every requirement has criteria; owner approves

phases.title: Design
phases.does: Components per repo, contracts, data, configuration, test plan; ADRs for real choices.

phases.title: Build
phases.does: One task, one branch, one pull request, tests first.

phases.title: Test
phases.does: Unit to end-to-end, every acceptance criterion passing.
phases.gate: Every criterion has a passing test

phases.title: Deploy
phases.does: Release notes, the pipeline, smoke test.
phases.gate: Smoke test passes in the target environment

phases.title: Maintain
phases.does: Runbook, incidents, feedback; new needs become a new intent.

flows.title: From a Jira ticket to an approved intent

steps.text: /intent <KEY> <slug> <JIRA-KEY> decides the intake kind is jira.
spec.py new creates specs/<KEY>-<slug>/ and records the intake (kind jira, ref).
The Atlassian MCP reads the initiative, its epics and stories, and the Confluence PRD.
The Figma MCP reads the linked design frames.
Each source is saved into inputs/ as a dated file, never edited afterwards.
intent.md is written from the sources only; anything they do not say goes to Open questions.
Existing code is involved, so /gap runs.
The gap-analyst agent maps the requirements onto the repos under code/: built, partial, missing, with file:line evidence.
Per area asked (architecture, localization, …): outputs/review/<area>.md and one row per finding in outputs/findings.json.
Gate: the product owner approves; spec.py approve <KEY> intent, then spec.py phase <KEY> spec.

flows.title: From an idea to an intent

steps.text: /intent <KEY> <slug> "<the idea>": intake kind idea, no ticket.
spec.py new creates the spec folder with intake idea.
The idea text is saved into inputs/.
intent.md: problem, who, outcome, success measures; unknowns as Open questions.
Gate: owner approves the intent.

flows.title: From a GitHub issue to an intent

steps.text: /intent <KEY> <slug> <org>/<repo>#<n>: intake kind github-issue.
gh issue view reads the issue, its labels and comments.
The issue snapshot goes to inputs/; intent.md is written from it.
/gap maps it onto the existing code.
gap-analyst reports what exists; findings land in outputs/findings.json.
/pr-review <org>/<repo>#<n>.
gh pr diff fetches the change.
The code-reviewer agent checks correctness and fit with the constitution and .claude/rules.
security-auditor also runs when auth, data, secrets or integrations changed.
If the PR belongs to a spec, each finding is appended to that spec's outputs/findings.json; then a merge / don't-merge verdict.
/feedback <KEY> with the reported issues; no personal data is copied.
The branch the reporter used comes from outputs/review/scope.md; the code path behind each issue is read.
Each issue gets a verdict (code, code likely, backend/data, other) and is linked to existing findings or added as a new one.
outputs/feedback/v<N>-<date>.md: summary, root cause and fix direction per issue, unknowns.
/fix-issue <the bug>.
Reproduce with a failing test, state the root cause in one sentence, make the smallest fix.
code-reviewer reviews the diff; its findings are addressed before commit.

flows.title: From an approved intent to production

steps.text: /spec: spec-writer turns the intent and stories into requirements with Given/When/Then criteria. Owner approves.
/design: architect designs components per repo, contracts, data and the test plan. Tech lead approves.
/tasks: one task, one branch, one pull request.
/build: the spec-gate hook blocks any edit under code/ until a spec is in build with intent, spec and design approved.
/test: test-writer adds tests until every acceptance criterion passes.
/deploy: release-manager prepares deploy order, migrations, rollback and release notes.
/maintain: runbook and incidents; security-auditor; new needs become a new intent.

delivers.d: intent, findings, spec, design, tasks, tests
one branch and one pull request per task
this portal: reads spec.py, never its own status

start.title: How to run the loop
start.lede: Everything starts in the engineering workspace with Claude Code, from VS Code or a terminal. Commands write files into specs/<KEY>-<slug>/; this hub reads those files. Status and approvals live only in spec.py.

steps.title: Get the workspace (first time only)
text: Clone the workspace, enable its git hooks, and follow its CLAUDE.md for the repos under code/ and the local .env.

commands.note: your GitHub access to the workspace repo

steps.title: Open Claude Code in the workspace
text: VS Code: File > Open Folder > the workspace, then open the Claude Code panel. Terminal: start claude inside the folder.
The session-start hook prints the specs in flight and their next step; the prompt router points you at the right command.

steps.title: Sign in to the tools (first time only)
text: Atlassian (Jira, Confluence) and Figma sign in with OAuth from /mcp. GitHub issues and pull requests use your gh login.

steps.title: Add a new work item
text: Use the builder above. The work key is the Jira initiative or epic key; the ticket (or idea, issue, PR) is the last argument, and /intent pulls it. For an idea without a ticket use a placeholder key such as IDEA-1.
/intent creates specs/<KEY>-<slug>/, saves every source into inputs/ and writes intent.md from the sources only; anything they do not say goes to Open questions.

commands.cmd: /intent IDEA-1 short-name "what we want and why"

steps.title: Review the existing code
text: /gap maps the intent onto the code, then reviews it area by area. Each area writes outputs/review/<area>.md and adds rows to outputs/findings.json. Classify the findings so they group by type, component and team.

commands.note: or one area: architecture, infra, apis, data, localization, ui-ux, security, tests

steps.title: Refresh and open the hub
text: The hub reads the workspace when you refresh it. The new work appears under Work with its findings dashboard and phase tabs.

steps.title: Approve
text: The owner reads the phase in the hub. Each phase awaiting approval shows an Approve box with the exact commands: approve, then move the spec to the next phase. Refresh the hub and the tab turns green. Approvals are recorded in status.json, in git, with who and when.

commands.cmd: python3 tools/spec.py approve PROJ-123 intent --by "<your name>"

steps.title: Spec, design, build, test, deploy
text: Each command writes its file and stops at a gate. The spec-gate hook blocks any edit under code/ until intent, spec and design are approved and the spec is in build. One task is one branch and one pull request.

steps.title: Feedback, bugs and pull requests
text: Customer or QA feedback becomes a batch with a root cause per issue, linked to findings. A single bug goes through /fix-issue. Any pull request goes through /pr-review.

steps.title: Where am I
text: /feature shows where a spec is and runs its next step. /handoff writes the resume state for the next session or a teammate.
